[34mInvestigated:[0m The compound formatter from commit d57cff2 in src/index.ts, including fmtCompound's handling of negatives, zero values and sub-second values. The README's "Time Format Written-Out" section, where the compound example had been placed. The existing compound tests in src/format.test.ts.

[33mLearned:[0m fmtCompound floors the absolute value to whole seconds, so milliseconds are dropped, and it returns "0s" when no parts remain, which also drops the sign for sub-second negatives such as -500 and -999. Days are the largest unit, so 400 days renders as "400d". The earlier round-trip test was ineffective: ms('1h 30m') returns NaN because parse() rejects spaced multi-unit input, so the assertion always passed. It has been removed.

[32mCompleted:[0m The README has a dedicated "Compound Format" section with examples and stated rules: space-separated parts, zero parts skipped, days as the largest unit, seconds as the smallest, a single leading minus for negatives, and compound taking precedence over long. src/format.test.ts gained tests for precedence over long, the compound: false path, rollover at each unit boundary, negative multi-unit values, fractional milliseconds, and throwing on NaN, Infinity and string input. The ineffective round-trip assertion was removed. The suite passes at 182 of 182 tests with 100% coverage, biome reports no issues and tsc --noEmit is clean. Nothing has been committed yet.

[35mNext Steps:[0m Waiting on the user's decision about whether to commit these changes. The open question is whether sub-second negatives such as -500 should keep a sign (for example "-0s" or "-500ms") instead of the current "0s".

[36mNotes:[0m The sign behaviour for sub-second negatives is now pinned by tests and documented in the README, so changing it means updating the tests and README together. The README placement under the written-out heading was corrected by moving the section.
